title: Files
description: Every file and folder of an artifact, as a front end may list them.

entries.description:
Each file and folder it holds, a folder before what it holds and
each folder's in the order of their names: a rule's one file alone.

manifest.description:
The file it is read from, as [`Contents`] takes it: a skill's
`SKILL.md`, or a rule's own file name. Said rather than left to a
front end, which would otherwise spell where each kind keeps what
it says.

truncated.description: Whether it holds more than [`FILES_CAP`], which `entries` stops at.

Kind.description: A kind of artifact, by the word a command line takes for it.

Listed.description: One file or folder of an artifact.

folder.description: Whether it is a folder, whose files are listed after it.

path.description:
Its route from the artifact's folder, `/` separated, as [`Contents`]
takes it; a rule's own file name. One whose name no route spells is
refused (`contents_name_unfit`) and listed by that name as near as
UTF-8 writes it, which another entry's can match: a refused entry is
shown, never asked for.

refused.description:
Why it is not followed, when it is not: a link leading out of the
holder, or back into a folder it is in, or something that does not
read. Listed all the same, since somebody looking for why a skill
misbehaves is looking for exactly that.

size.description:
How many bytes a file holds; none for a folder, and for one not
followed.

Said.description:
An error as a serialized type holds one: its code, for a front end to act
on, and its message, for whoever reads it.

Built where the type is serialized, or kept in what a front end reads
(the workspace's snapshot), in place of the error, since an error
holds what JSON has no shape for (an `io::Error`, a parser's own), and
only these two are meant to leave core. Its fields are public for a
front end that reads the snapshot as Rust rather than as JSON, the TUI.

message.description:
Written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as every URL
is: an error can quote one, a source's among them, and what built
the error is no promise that it carries no credential.
